symbols.def: The fixed penalty on squared standardized imbalance.

symbols.def: The history records own-treatment and group-saturation exposures over all \(2B\) experimental periods.

symbols.name: Y_{gti}
symbols.def: The endpoint response of unit \(i\) in group \(g\) at time \(t\) under a complete within-group exposure path.

symbols.name: Y_{gbi}(d,q)
symbols.def: \(Y_{gbi}(d,q)=Y_{g,2b,i}(h)\) for any \(h\in\mathcal H_{2B}\) whose entries at periods \(2b-1\) and \(2b\) both equal \((d,q)\); ordinary nonanticipation and the imposed lag-one finite-memory restriction make this value invariant to the remaining entries.

symbols.name: \mathcal F_b
symbols.def: \(\mathcal F_b\) is generated by assignments and observed endpoints through block \(b\).

symbols.type: observed group mean at block endpoint

symbols.name: \bar Y^{\mathrm{obs}}_b
symbols.type: observed grand group mean at block endpoint

symbols.name: H_g
symbols.def: A prespecified centered group covariate score.

symbols.name: A_{gbi}
symbols.def: Conditionally on \(x_b\), exactly \(nQ_{gb}\) units are sampled uniformly without replacement in group \(g\), independently across groups, and assigned treatment one at both periods of block \(b\); the remaining units receive zero.

symbols.name: \pi_{k\ell,b}
symbols.def: For exposure cells \(k\) and \(\ell\) in block \(b\), \(\pi_{k\ell,b}=\Pr(I_kI_\ell=1\mid\mathcal F_{b-1})\), with \(\pi_{kk,b}=\pi_{k,b}\); these known probabilities are logged by the randomizer.

symbols.name: \tau_b
symbols.def: \(\tau_b=(Gn)^{-1}\sum_{g,i,d,q}c_{dq}Y_{gbi}(d,q)\), where the sums range over \(\mathcal G_G\), \(\mathcal I_n\), \(\mathcal D\), and \(\mathcal Q\).

symbols.type: balanced-sign component of the block score

symbols.name: U_b
symbols.type: within-group component of the block score

symbols.name: (A_b^\star,W_b^\star)
symbols.def: A centered Gaussian vector with the exact conditional \(P_0\)-covariance of \((A_b,W_b)\), supported on that covariance range when singular.

symbols.name: (R_b^\star,W_b^\star)
symbols.def: A centered Gaussian vector with the exact conditional \(P_0\)-covariance of \((R_b,W_b)\), supported on that covariance range when singular.

symbols.name: \mathcal K_b
symbols.def: Each \(k=(g,i,d,q)\in\mathcal K_b\) indexes one potential exposure cell in block \(b\).

symbols.name: \widehat\Gamma_b
symbols.def: The pairwise Horvitz--Thompson covariance sum augmented by a diagonal completion for \(\mathcal Z_b\).

assumptions.condition: Conditional on the finite population \(\{Y_{gti}:g\in\mathcal G_G,\ i\in\mathcal I_n\}\), the only randomness is generated by \(x_b\) and \(A_{gbi}\).
For every unit, \(Y_{gti}\) is invariant to treatment and saturation assignments outside group \(g\).
Within group \(g\), the endpoint response depends on the contemporaneous assignment vector only through the unit's own treatment \(d\) and the realized saturation \(q\).
For every \(t\leq2B\), if \(h,h'\in\mathcal H_{2B}\) agree through period \(t\), then \(Y_{gti}(h)=Y_{gti}(h')\); assignments after period \(t\) do not affect the period-\(t\) endpoint.
For every \(2\leq t\leq2B\), if \(h,h'\in\mathcal H_{2B}\) agree at periods \(t-1\) and \(t\), then \(Y_{gti}(h)=Y_{gti}(h')\) regardless of the remaining history entries.

novel.justification: This is an imposed finite-memory restriction, not a consequence of ordinary nonanticipation. It is interpretable when saturation and own treatment are held fixed within each two-period block, so the endpoint depends on the block's sustained exposure while earlier blocks may affect the predictable randomization rule but not the endpoint response.

assumptions.condition: Uniformly over \(b\in\mathcal B_B\) and realized \(\mathcal F_{b-1}\), \(c_\sigma\leq\sigma_b^2\leq C_\sigma\).

novel.justification: This is an imposed predictable-array stabilization condition for the history-adaptive sequence. Li--Ding--Rubin (2018) motivates the static projection analogy but does not state this adaptive block-average hypothesis.

definitions.name: bounded lag-one partial-interference triangular-array class
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal M_{G,B}=\{(Y,H):G\in2\mathbb N,\ B\in\mathbb N,\ n\in4\mathbb N,\ \text{assumptions }\texttt{ass:design-based-finiteness},\texttt{ass:partial-interference},\texttt{ass:stratified-interference},\texttt{ass:nonanticipation},\texttt{ass:finite-memory-lag-one},\texttt{ass:imbalance-variance-window},\texttt{ass:rr-covariance-stabilization},\texttt{ass:rr-limit-positive},\texttt{ass:cr-covariance-stabilization},\texttt{ass:projection-stabilization}\text{ hold}\}\).

definitions.name: predictable complement-symmetric soft rerandomization
definitions.construction: At block \(b\), draw \(x_b\in\mathcal X_G\) with \(P_{\mathrm{RR},b}(x\mid\mathcal F_{b-1})=P_0(x)f_{\eta,\kappa}\{W_b(x)\}/C_b\); set \(Q_{gb}=q_H\) for \(x_{gb}=1\) and \(q_L\) otherwise; then draw exactly \(nQ_{gb}\) treated units uniformly and independently within each group and hold both stages fixed for the two periods.

definitions.name: perfect-matching handle for singular weighted Gaussian transport
definitions.construction: Represent the balanced three-vector \((a_{gb,1},a_{gb,2},V_{gb}/\sigma_b)\) by a uniform random perfect matching followed by independent pair orientations; target a history-uniform covariance-range comparison through smooth Lindeberg replacement, covariance interpolation, fourth-moment truncation, and a conditional characteristic-function augmentation for \(U_b\).

definitions.name: observable Young-completed covariance estimator
definitions.construction: \(\widehat\Gamma_b=(Gn^2)^{-1}[\sum_{k,\ell:\pi_{k\ell,b}>0}I_kI_\ell(\pi_{k\ell,b}-\pi_{k,b}\pi_{\ell,b})u_{k,b}u_{\ell,b}^\top/(\pi_{k\ell,b}\pi_{k,b}\pi_{\ell,b})+\sum_{\{k,\ell\}\in\mathcal Z_b}\{I_ku_{k,b}u_{k,b}^\top/\pi_{k,b}+I_\ell u_{\ell,b}u_{\ell,b}^\top/\pi_{\ell,b}\}]\), followed by block averaging and eigenvalue clipping at \(r_B\).

definitions.name: alternating-block genuinely adaptive finite-population witness
definitions.construction: For \(G\in4\mathbb N\), represent the four sign pairs \((H_g,J_g)\in\{-1,1\}^2\) equally often and set \(\lambda=1\). On type A blocks take \((a_{Dg},a_{Sg})=(H_g,J_g)\) and \(L=0\); on type B blocks take \((a_{Dg},a_{Sg})=(J_g,H_g)\) and \(L=4\). Set \(\theta_g=4a_{Dg}\), \(\delta_g=L-\theta_g\), \(h_g=a_{Sg}/2+a_{Dg}-L/2\), and \(Y_{gbi}(d,q)=h_g+d(\delta_g+\theta_gq)\).

statements.statement: For every finite \(G\), \(B\), and history, complement symmetry gives \(\Pr_{\mathrm{RR}}(Q_{gb}=q_H\mid\mathcal F_{b-1})=\Pr_{\mathrm{RR}}(Q_{gb}=q_L\mid\mathcal F_{b-1})=1/2\). Hence \(\pi_{gbi,dq}=p_{dq}/2\geq1/8\) and \(\mathbb E_{\mathrm{RR}}(\widehat\tau)=\tau\) exactly.
statements.justification: Exact first-order symmetry prevents adaptive normalizers from creating bias or hidden first-order weights.
statements.gap: YuMaLiu2025 Theorem 3 treats a fixed minimax two-stage design, while LiZhao2026Adaptive Theorem 1 treats single-stage logged propensities; neither proves this two-stage complement-symmetric adaptive identity.
statements.consumer: A prospective multigroup market experiment can log the adaptive kernel and retain an exactly interpretable joint sustained-exposure target.
statements.proof_tex:
Fix a block \(b\) and condition on \(\mathcal F_{b-1}\).  By the definition of \(\mathcal X_G\), the map \(x\mapsto-x\) is a bijection of \(\mathcal X_G\), and \(P_0(-x)=P_0(x)\).  Since \(Z_b(-x)=-Z_b(x)\), also \(W_b(-x)=-W_b(x)\).  The weight is even, because
\[
 f_{\eta,\kappa}(-w)=\eta+(1-\eta)e^{-\kappa(-w)^2}=f_{\eta,\kappa}(w).
\]
Consequently \(P_{\mathrm{RR},b}(-x\mid\mathcal F_{b-1})=P_{\mathrm{RR},b}(x\mid\mathcal F_{b-1})\).  Pairing every \(x\) with \(-x\) gives
\[
 \Pr(x_{gb}=1\mid\mathcal F_{b-1})
 =\Pr(x_{gb}=-1\mid\mathcal F_{b-1})=\frac12.
\]
The definition of \(Q_{gb}\) proves the two asserted saturation probabilities.

Conditional on \(Q_{gb}=q\), the fixed-count simple random sample includes unit \(i\) with probability \(q\) when \(d=1\) and with probability \(1-q\) when \(d=0\).  Thus, by the preceding first-stage calculation and the definition of \(p_{dq}\),
\[
 \pi_{gbi,dq}
 =\Pr(Q_{gb}=q\mid\mathcal F_{b-1})
   \Pr(A_{gbi}=d\mid Q_{gb}=q,\mathcal F_{b-1})
 =\frac{p_{dq}}2.
\]
Since \(q_L=1/4\) and \(q_H=3/4\), \(p_{dq}\geq1/4\), whence \(\pi_{gbi,dq}\geq1/8\), so every division in the Horvitz--Thompson estimator is valid.

Assumptions \(\texttt{ass:partial-interference}\), \(\texttt{ass:stratified-interference}\), \(\texttt{ass:nonanticipation}\), and \(\texttt{ass:finite-memory-lag-one}\) imply consistency at the endpoint of the held two-period block:
\[
 I_{gbi,dq}Y^{\mathrm{obs}}_{g,2b,i}
 =I_{gbi,dq}Y_{gbi}(d,q).
\]
The potential endpoint on the right is fixed under \(\texttt{ass:design-based-finiteness}\).  Therefore
\[
 \mathbb E\!\left[
   \frac{I_{gbi,dq}Y^{\mathrm{obs}}_{g,2b,i}}{\pi_{gbi,dq}}
   \mathrel{\bigg|}\mathcal F_{b-1}\right]
 =Y_{gbi}(d,q).
\]
Summing this equality with coefficient \(c_{dq}/(Gn)\) proves
\(\mathbb E(\widehat\tau_b\mid\mathcal F_{b-1})=\tau_b\).  Iterated expectation and block averaging then give
\[
 \mathbb E(\widehat\tau)
 =\frac1B\sum_{b=1}^B\mathbb E(\widehat\tau_b)
 =\frac1B\sum_{b=1}^B\tau_b=\tau.
\]

statements.statement: For every block, \(R_b=A_b+U_b\), \(\mathbb E(U_b\mid x_b,\mathcal F_{b-1})=0\), and the group summands of \(U_b\) are conditionally independent. Consequently \(\Sigma_{b,\mathrm{RR}}=\operatorname{Var}_{\mathrm{RR}}(A_b\mid\mathcal F_{b-1})+K_b\), the cross covariance is zero, and exactly the same \(K_b\) appears under \(P_0\).
statements.justification: This exact split isolates the only covariance component that the first-stage soft tilt can change.
statements.gap: JiangImaiMalani2023 derives static two-stage covariance formulas, but not this predictable balanced-sign decomposition with unchanged fixed-count within-group covariance.
statements.consumer: The decomposition is the algebraic bridge from the adaptive design to the projection-efficiency theorem and the observable studentizer.
statements.proof_tex:
Fix \(b\) and condition on \(\mathcal F_{b-1}\).  The complement-symmetry calculation from \(\texttt{def:soft-two-stage-design}\) gives \(\pi_{gbi,dq}=p_{dq}/2\).  Only the realized saturation contributes and hence
\[
 \sqrt G\,\widehat\tau_b
 =\frac{2}{\sqrt G}\sum_{g=1}^G\widehat m_{gb,Q_{gb}}.
\]
On the other hand, the definition of \(m_{gbq}\) gives
\[
 \sqrt G\,\tau_b
 =\frac1{\sqrt G}\sum_{g=1}^G(m_{gbq_L}+m_{gbq_H}).
\]
For \(x_{gb}=1\), the difference between twice the selected mean and the sum of the two means is \(a_{gb}\); for \(x_{gb}=-1\), it is \(-a_{gb}\).  Substituting \(\widehat m_{gbq}=m_{gbq}+e_{gbq}\) therefore yields, exactly,
\[
 R_b=\frac1{\sqrt G}\sum_gx_{gb}a_{gb}
       +\frac2{\sqrt G}\sum_ge_{gb,Q_{gb}}=A_b+U_b.
\]

Within a group, fixed-count simple random sampling and the definition of \(p_{dq}\) imply \(\mathbb E(\widehat m_{gbq}\mid Q_{gb}=q,\mathcal F_{b-1})=m_{gbq}\).  Thus
\[
 \mathbb E(e_{gb,Q_{gb}}\mid x_b,\mathcal F_{b-1})=0,
 \qquad
 \mathbb E(U_b\mid x_b,\mathcal F_{b-1})=0.
\]
The second-stage samples are independent across groups conditional on \(x_b\), so the summands of \(U_b\) are conditionally independent.  It follows by conditional covariance additivity that
\[
 \operatorname{Var}(U_b\mid x_b,\mathcal F_{b-1})
 =\frac4G\sum_gT_{gb,Q_{gb}}.
\]
The conditional mean-zero identity also gives
\(\operatorname{Cov}(A_b,U_b\mid\mathcal F_{b-1})=0\).  Complement symmetry makes each \(Q_{gb}\) marginally high or low with probability \(1/2\), both under the soft law and under \(P_0\).  Hence under either first-stage law
\[
 \mathbb E\{\operatorname{Var}(U_b\mid x_b,\mathcal F_{b-1})
          \mid\mathcal F_{b-1}\}
 =\frac2G\sum_g(T_{gbq_L}+T_{gbq_H})=K_b.
\]
The law of total covariance now proves
\[
 \Sigma_{b,\mathrm{RR}}
 =\operatorname{Var}_{\mathrm{RR}}(A_b\mid\mathcal F_{b-1})+K_b,
\]
with zero cross covariance, and proves that precisely the same \(K_b\) is present under \(P_0\).

statements.statement: The block scores satisfy \(\mathbb E(R_b\mid\mathcal F_{b-1})=0\), and \(\sqrt{GB}(\widehat\tau-\tau)=B^{-1/2}\sum_{b\in\mathcal B_B}R_b\).
statements.justification: Predictable centering makes the across-block accumulation a design-based martingale rather than a pseudo-target drift.
statements.gap: LiZhao2026Adaptive supplies the single-stage martingale template, while the present score has dependent two-stage exposure categories and lagged potential outcomes.
statements.consumer: This identity supplies the filtration structure needed for the root-\(GB\) limit law.
statements.proof_tex:
By \(\texttt{prop:exact-unbiasedness}\), conditional on \(\mathcal F_{b-1}\), \(\mathbb E(\widehat\tau_b\mid\mathcal F_{b-1})=\tau_b\).  Assumptions \(\texttt{ass:nonanticipation}\) and \(\texttt{ass:finite-memory-lag-one}\) ensure that \(\tau_b\), which uses the two-period sustained-exposure endpoints of block \(b\), is a fixed finite-population contrast rather than a function of the current random draw.  Therefore
\[
 \mathbb E(R_b\mid\mathcal F_{b-1})
 =\sqrt G\{\mathbb E(\widehat\tau_b\mid\mathcal F_{b-1})-\tau_b\}=0.
\]
Moreover, the definitions of \(\widehat\tau\), \(\tau\), and \(R_b\) give the pathwise identity
\[
 \sqrt{GB}(\widehat\tau-\tau)
 =\frac{\sqrt{GB}}B\sum_{b=1}^B(\widehat\tau_b-\tau_b)
 =B^{-1/2}\sum_{b=1}^BR_b.
\]

statements.statement: There exists a finite constant \(C_R\), independent of \(G\), \(B\), \(b\), and the history, such that \(\mathbb E_0\|R_b\|^4\leq C_R\) and \(\mathbb E_{\mathrm{RR}}(\|R_b\|^4\mid\mathcal F_{b-1})\leq C_R/\eta\).
statements.justification: The uniform fourth moment supplies the actual conditional Lindeberg control rather than treating covariance stabilization as a substitute.
statements.gap: LiDing2017FPCLT gives finite-population leverage conditions, but not likelihood-ratio transfer of a joint two-stage score under a predictable soft tilt.
statements.consumer: The martingale central limit theorem uses this bound to control every Cram\'er--Wold contrast.
statements.proof_tex:
All constants below may depend on the fixed constants \(M\), \(n\), \(q_L\), and \(q_H\), but not on \(G\), \(B\), \(b\), or the realized history.  The fixed contrast coefficients and \(|Y_{gbi}(d,q)|\leq M\) give constants \(L_a,L_e<\infty\) such that
\[
 \|a_{gb}\|\leq L_a,
 \qquad \|e_{gbq}\|\leq L_e
\]
for all indices.  The second inequality also follows uniformly if \(n\) varies through \(4\mathbb N\), because \(p_{dq}\geq1/4\) and every term is an average of bounded endpoints.

Generate a uniform balanced sign vector by first drawing a uniform perfect matching of \(\{1,\ldots,G\}\), and then, independently for each matched pair \(\{r_j,s_j\}\), assigning opposite signs with a Rademacher orientation \(\xi_j\).  Every balanced sign vector is compatible with exactly \((G/2)!\) such oriented matchings, so this construction has law \(P_0\).  Conditional on the matching,
\[
 A_b=G^{-1/2}\sum_{j=1}^{G/2}\xi_j(a_{r_jb}-a_{s_jb}).
\]
For a scalar Rademacher sum, expansion of the fourth power and cancellation of monomials containing an odd power of some \(\xi_j\) give
\[
 \mathbb E\left(\sum_j\xi_jd_j\right)^4
 =\sum_jd_j^4+6\sum_{j<k}d_j^2d_k^2
 \leq3\left(\sum_jd_j^2\right)^2.
\]
Applying this to each coordinate and using norm equivalence in \(\mathbb R^2\) proves \(\mathbb E_0\|A_b\|^4\leq C_A\).

Conditional on \(x_b\), the group terms in \(U_b\) are independent, centered, and bounded by \(2L_e/\sqrt G\).  The same fourth-power expansion, now with expectations in place of Rademacher averages, gives
\[
 \mathbb E(\|U_b\|^4\mid x_b,\mathcal F_{b-1})\leq C_U.
\]
Since \(\|u+v\|^4\leq8(\|u\|^4+\|v\|^4)\), \(\texttt{lem:score-decomposition}\) yields
\[
 \mathbb E_0\|R_b\|^4\leq C_R
\]
for a finite uniform \(C_R\).  Finally,
\[
 \frac{dP_{\mathrm{RR},b}}{dP_0}(x\mid\mathcal F_{b-1})
 =\frac{f_{\eta,\kappa}(W_b(x))}{C_b}leq\frac1\eta,
\]
because \(f_{\eta,\kappa}\leq1\) and \(C_b\geq\eta\).  Conditional second-stage laws are identical under the two designs, so likelihood-ratio domination gives
\[
 \mathbb E_{\mathrm{RR}}(\|R_b\|^4\mid\mathcal F_{b-1})
 \leq C_R/\eta.
\]

statements.statement: There is a constant \(C_\pi<\infty\), independent of block and history, such that for distinct groups \(g\neq h\), \(\left|\mathbb E_{\mathrm{RR}}(x_{gb}x_{hb}\mid\mathcal F_{b-1})\right|\leq C_\pi/G\). Therefore every feasible cross-group exposure-pair probability equals its product-marginal benchmark plus \(O(G^{-1})\) uniformly, while every feasible within-group pair probability is bounded away from zero.
statements.justification: Uniform pair control turns the exact PSD completion identity into a concentrating observable matrix estimator.
statements.gap: Static two-stage variance papers compute pair probabilities directly; predictable soft weighting requires a new mixed finite-difference bound under the fixed-half support.
statements.consumer: The bound controls the \(O(G^2)\) cross-group terms in the conservative covariance estimator.
statements.proof_tex:
Fix distinct groups \(g\neq h\), condition on \(\mathcal F_{b-1}\), and use the uniform perfect-matching representation.  The event that \(g\) is paired with \(h\) has probability \(1/(G-1)\), and its contribution to \(|\mathbb E_0[x_gx_hf_{\eta,\kappa}(W_b)]|\) is therefore at most \(1/(G-1)\).

On the complementary event, \(g\) and \(h\) lie in two different matching pairs.  Conditional on all other orientations, write
\[
 W_b=S+\xi r+\zeta s,
\]
where \(\xi,\zeta\) are the two independent orientations.  From \(|V_{gb}|\leq K_H+2\lambda M\) and \(\sigma_b^2\geq c_\sigma\),
\[
 |r|\vee|s|\leq\frac{2(K_H+2\lambda M)}{\sqrt{Gc_\sigma}}.
\]
The conditional expectation of \(x_gx_hf_{\eta,\kappa}(W_b)\) is, up to a sign, one quarter of the mixed difference
\[
 f(S+r+s)-f(S+r-s)-f(S-r+s)+f(S-r-s).
\]
Twice applying the fundamental theorem of calculus bounds its absolute value by
\(4\|f_{\eta,\kappa}''\|_\infty|rs|\leq C/G\).  Averaging the two matching cases yields
\[
 |\mathbb E_0[x_gx_hf_{\eta,\kappa}(W_b)]|\leq C/G.
\]
Since \(C_b\geq\eta\), division by the soft-kernel normalizer gives
\[
 |\mathbb E_{\mathrm{RR}}(x_{gb}x_{hb}\mid\mathcal F_{b-1})|
 \leq C_\pi/G.
\]

Complement symmetry gives \(\mathbb E_{\mathrm{RR}}x_{gb}=0\).  Thus, for \(s,t\in\{-1,1\}\),
\[
 \Pr(x_{gb}=s,x_{hb}=t\mid\mathcal F_{b-1})
 =\frac14\{1+st\,\mathbb E_{mathrm{RR}}(x_{gb}x_{hb}\mid\mathcal F_{b-1})\}
 =\frac14+O(G^{-1}).
\]
Conditional on the two saturations, the within-group samples are independent across groups.  Multiplication by the appropriate factors \(p_{dq}\) and \(p_{er}\), each at least \(1/4\), proves the uniform product-marginal approximation for every cross-group exposure pair.

For a feasible pair within one group, the first-stage factor is \(1/2\).  The second-stage factor is one of the simple-random-sampling probabilities
\[
 q,\quad 1-q,\quad
 \frac{nq(nq-1)}{n(n-1)},\quad
 \frac{n(1-q)\{n(1-q)-1\}}{n(n-1)},\quad
 \frac{nq\,n(1-q)}{n(n-1)}.
\]
Terms equal to zero are precisely infeasible pairs.  Over \(n\in4\mathbb N\) and \(q\in\{1/4,3/4\}\), every positive displayed term is bounded below by a universal positive constant (the smallest two-treated boundary occurs at \(n=8\)).  This proves the final assertion.

statements.statement:
For every sequence of finite-population designs belonging to \(\mathcal M_{G,B}\) along which \(B\to\infty\), with the admissible even value of \(G\) allowed to depend arbitrarily on \(B\) and in particular allowed to remain fixed,
\[
\sqrt{GB}(\widehat\tau-\tau)=B^{-1/2}\sum_{b\in\mathcal B_B}R_b\ \Rightarrow\ N_2(0,\Omega_{\mathrm{RR}}).
\]
Thus the root-\(GB\) limit law requires no restriction on \(G/B\); it is derived from martingale centering, the uniform block fourth-moment bound, and predictable covariance stabilization with a positive-definite limit.
statements.justification: The root-\(GB\) joint law shows that repeated predictable blocks accumulate valid randomization information even when the number of groups is fixed.
statements.gap: Yu--Ma--Liu permits broad center/time regimes but studies a fixed minimax schedule, while Li--Zhao treats general single-stage adaptive scores; neither derives this joint fixed-count spillover-and-carryover martingale law under outcome-adaptive soft rerandomization.
statements.consumer: Prospective multigroup online experiments obtain joint direct-and-spillover inference from many blocks without requiring the number of groups to grow.
statements.proof_tex:
Fix any sequence in the proposed statement and any \(t\in\mathbb R^2\).  No step below requires \(G\to\infty\), so \(G\) may be fixed, bounded and varying, or divergent.  If \(t=0\), the asserted scalar projection is identically zero.  Suppose henceforth that \(t\ne0\), and define
\[
 \xi_{Bb}=B^{-1/2}t^\top R_b,
 \qquad
 \mathcal V_B=\sum_{b=1}^B
   \mathbb E(\xi_{Bb}^2\mid\mathcal F_{b-1}),
 \qquad
 V_B=\mathbb E\mathcal V_B.
\]
By \(\texttt{lem:martingale-centering}\), \(\{\xi_{Bb},\mathcal F_b:1\le b\le B\}\) is a martingale-difference array.  By the definition of \(\Sigma_{b,\mathrm{RR}}\),
\[
 \mathcal V_B
 =t^\top\left(B^{-1}\sum_{b=1}^B\Sigma_{b,\mathrm{RR}}\right)t.
\]
Therefore \(\texttt{ass:rr-covariance-stabilization}\) gives
\[
 \mathcal V_B\longrightarrow_P v_t,
 \qquad
 v_t:=t^\top\Omega_{\mathrm{RR}}t.                         \tag{1}
\]
Assumption \(\texttt{ass:rr-limit-positive}\) implies \(v_t>0\).

The fourth-moment bound in \(\texttt{lem:block-moments}\), conditional on each realized history, gives a constant \(C_t<\infty\), independent of \(B\), \(G\), the block, and the history, for which
\[
 \sum_{b=1}^B\mathbb E(\xi_{Bb}^4\mid\mathcal F_{b-1})
 =B^{-2}\sum_{b=1}^B
   \mathbb E\{(t^\top R_b)^4\mid\mathcal F_{b-1}\}
 \le \frac{C_t}{B}.                                       \tag{2}
\]
The conditional Cauchy--Schwarz inequality and the same bound also imply
\[
 t^\top\Sigma_{b,\mathrm{RR}}t
 =\mathbb E\{(t^\top R_b)^2\mid\mathcal F_{b-1}\}
 \le C_t^{1/2}.                                            \tag{3}
\]
Thus \(0\le\mathcal V_B\le C_t^{1/2}\) almost surely.  The boundedness in (3) makes \(\{\mathcal V_B\}\) uniformly integrable, so (1) yields
\[
 V_B\longrightarrow v_t,
 \qquad
 \frac{\mathcal V_B}{V_B}\longrightarrow_P1.             \tag{4}
\]
In particular, \(V_B>0\) for all sufficiently large \(B\).

We next derive, rather than assume, the Lindeberg condition in \(\texttt{lem:li-zhao-martingale-clt}\).  For every \(\epsilon>0\), the elementary inequality \(z^2\mathbf1\{|z|\ge a\}\le z^4/a^2\), used with \(a=\epsilon V_B^{-1/2}\), gives
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 &V_B^{-1}\sum_{b=1}^B
  \mathbb E\left[\xi_{Bb}^2
   \mathbf1\{|\xi_{Bb}|\ge\epsilon V_B^{-1/2}\}\right]\\
 &\qquad\le
 \epsilon^{-2}\sum_{b=1}^B\mathbb E(\xi_{Bb}^4)
 \le \frac{C_t}{\epsilon^2B}\longrightarrow0,             \tag{5}
 \end{aligned}
\]
where the last inequality follows by taking expectations in (2).  Equations (4)--(5) verify every normalization and Lindeberg premise of \(\texttt{lem:li-zhao-martingale-clt}\).  Consequently
\[
 V_B^{-1/2}\sum_{b=1}^B\xi_{Bb}\Rightarrow N(0,1).
\]
Combining this conclusion with \(V_B\to v_t\) in (4) gives
\[
 t^\top B^{-1/2}\sum_{b=1}^BR_b
 \Rightarrow N(0,t^\top\Omega_{\mathrm{RR}}t).             \tag{6}
\]
Since (6) holds for every \(t\in\mathbb R^2\), all one-dimensional characteristic functions of the vector on the left converge to
\(\exp\{-t^\top\Omega_{\mathrm{RR}}t/2\}\), the characteristic function of \(N_2(0,\Omega_{\mathrm{RR}})\).  This proves the asserted bivariate convergence.  Finally,
\[
 \sqrt{GB}(\widehat\tau-\tau)
 =B^{-1/2}\sum_{b=1}^BR_b
\]
is the exact identity in \(\texttt{lem:martingale-centering}\).  The constants in (2)--(3) are uniform in \(G\), and the only diverging denominator used in (2) and (5) is \(B\); hence no relative-growth condition has entered the proof.

statements.statement:
As \(G\to\infty\), uniformly over blocks and histories and without any restriction on \(G/B\), \(\Sigma_{b,\mathrm{RR}}=\Sigma_{b,0}-(1-v_{\eta,\kappa})\beta_b\beta_b^\top+o(1)\). Along every sequence with \(G\to\infty\) on which the complete-randomization, soft-rerandomization, and projection covariance stabilizations hold,
\[
\Omega_{\mathrm{RR}}=\Omega_{\mathrm{CR}}-(1-v_{\eta,\kappa})P.
\]
For every fixed contrast \(c\in\mathbb R^2\setminus\{0\}\), soft rerandomization has strictly smaller asymptotic variance than complete randomization if and only if \(c^\top Pc>0\).
statements.justification: The identity names the exact precision gain and characterizes all and only the improved causal contrasts.
statements.gap: LiDingRubin2018 Theorem 1 gives a static hard-truncation scalar ATE decomposition; this theorem targets a predictable soft tilt, a joint direct-and-spillover vector, fixed-half group saturations, and unchanged second-stage sampling noise.
statements.consumer: The population criterion classifies which scientifically chosen direct-spillover contrasts gain asymptotic precision in theoretical design comparisons and fully specified simulation calibrations.

statements.statement:
For every block, \(\mathbb E(\widehat\Gamma_b\mid\mathcal F_{b-1})=\Sigma_{b,\mathrm{RR}}+D_b\) with \(D_b\succeq0\).  Along every sequence in \(\mathcal M_{G,B}\) with \(B\to\infty\) and arbitrary admissible even \(G\), including fixed \(G\),
\[
\widehat\Gamma=\Omega_{\mathrm{RR}}+B^{-1}\sum_{b\in\mathcal B_B}D_b+o_P(1).
\]
The block matrices are uniformly bounded in Frobenius norm.  Every probability limit point of \(\widehat\Gamma\) therefore dominates \(\Omega_{\mathrm{RR}}\) in Loewner order; moreover, clipping is inactive with probability tending to one and \(\|\widehat\Gamma_+^{-1}\|=O_P(1)\).
statements.justification: The matrix completion handles impossible joint exposure cells, and its block averaging remains valid with fixed or growing group count.
statements.gap: Jiang--Imai--Malani provides conservative covariance estimators for static two-stage designs; the present identity and many-block concentration result cover logged history-dependent pair probabilities and matrix, rather than coordinatewise, conservativeness.
statements.consumer: The completed matrix supports simultaneous inference after many adaptive blocks even when some within-group exposure pairs can never be jointly observed.
statements.proof_tex:
Fix a block and condition throughout on \(\mathcal F_{b-1}\).  The fixed potential outcomes make each \(u_{k,b}\) nonrandom under this conditioning, and the logged first- and second-order probabilities are denoted by \(\pi_k:=\pi_{k,b}\) and \(\pi_{k\ell}:=\pi_{k\ell,b}\).  The definitions of the causal block target and the Horvitz--Thompson block estimator give the exact representation
\[
 R_b=\frac1{\sqrt G\,n}\sum_{k\in\mathcal K_b}
       \left(\frac{I_k}{\pi_k}-1\right)u_{k,b}.             \tag{7}
\]
All divisions in (7) are valid.  Indeed, complementation preserves \(P_0\), sends \(W_b(x)\) to \(-W_b(x)\), and leaves the even function \(f_{\eta,\kappa}\{W_b(x)\}\) unchanged.  Pairing every balanced assignment with its complement therefore gives conditional first-stage saturation probability \(1/2\).  Since \(p_{dq}\ge1/4\), the two-stage definition gives \(\pi_k=p_{dq}/2\ge1/8\).  Taking the conditional covariance of (7) and using
\(\mathbb E(I_kI_\ell\mid\mathcal F_{b-1})=\pi_{k\ell}\) yields
\[
 \Sigma_{b,\mathrm{RR}}
 =\frac1{Gn^2}\sum_{k,\ell\in\mathcal K_b}
   \frac{\pi_{k\ell}-\pi_k\pi_\ell}{\pi_k\pi_\ell}
   u_{k,b}u_{\ell,b}^\top.                                 \tag{8}
\]

If \(\pi_{k\ell}>0\), conditional expectation of the corresponding summand in \(\widehat\Gamma_b\) replaces \(I_kI_\ell\) by \(\pi_{k\ell}\), exactly recovering its ordered-pair term in (8).  If \(k\ne\ell\) and \(\pi_{k\ell}=0\), the two ordered terms for \((k,\ell)\) and \((\ell,k)\) in (8) equal
\[
 -u_{k,b}u_{\ell,b}^\top-u_{\ell,b}u_{k,b}^\top.
\]
For the corresponding unordered pair, the completion in \(\widehat\Gamma_b\) has conditional expectation
\(u_{k,b}u_{k,b}^\top+u_{\ell,b}u_{\ell,b}^\top\).  Its excess over the two missing covariance terms is therefore
\[
 (u_{k,b}+u_{\ell,b})(u_{k,b}+u_{\ell,b})^\top\succeq0.   \tag{9}
\]
Summing (9) over \(\mathcal Z_b\), with the normalization in \(\texttt{def:completed-studentizer}\), proves
\[
 \mathbb E(\widehat\Gamma_b\mid\mathcal F_{b-1})
 =\Sigma_{b,\mathrm{RR}}+D_b,
 \qquad D_b\succeq0.                                      \tag{10}
\]
The completion is observable because it uses only realized cell outcomes and logged design probabilities.  It introduces no unobserved cross-potential-outcome product.

We record why the matrices in (10) are uniformly bounded even when \(G\) does not diverge.  The outcome envelope and the fixed contrast coefficients give \(\sup_{k,b}\|u_{k,b}\|<\infty\).  By \(\texttt{lem:pair-probability-control}\), for all sufficiently large \(G\), feasible cross-group pair probabilities are bounded away from zero and their covariance coefficients are \(O(G^{-1})\), whereas feasible within-group pair probabilities are bounded away from zero.  There are \(O(G^2n^2)\) ordered cross-group pairs, each carrying after the outer normalization a coefficient of order \(O(G^{-2}n^{-2})\), and \(O(Gn^2)\) within-group pairs, each carrying a coefficient of order \(O(G^{-1}n^{-2})\).  The impossible-pair completion has the same bounded count-normalization product.  The finitely many smaller admissible values of \(G\) are also uniformly controlled: \(f_{\eta,\kappa}\ge\eta>0\) gives the soft law the same finite first-stage support as \(P_0\), and the fixed-count second stage has a positive minimum over every feasible cell pair.  Hence there is a constant \(C_\Gamma<\infty\), independent of \(B\), \(G\), the block, and the realized history, such that
\[
 \|\widehat\Gamma_b\|_F+\|D_b\|_F\le C_\Gamma.           \tag{11}
\]
Because the soft weight is strictly positive on all of \(\mathcal X_G\), the zero-pair set is the zero-pair set of the underlying balanced first stage and fixed-count second stage; it does not depend on the numerical, history-dependent tilt.  Thus the fixed potential outcomes make \(D_b\) deterministic.

Put
\[
 M_b=\widehat\Gamma_b-
     \mathbb E(\widehat\Gamma_b\mid\mathcal F_{b-1}).
\]
Then \(\{M_b,\mathcal F_b\}\) is an entrywise matrix martingale-difference sequence.  Conditional orthogonality across distinct blocks and (11) give
\[
 \mathbb E\left\|B^{-1}\sum_{b=1}^BM_b\right\|_F^2
 =B^{-2}\sum_{b=1}^B\mathbb E\|M_b\|_F^2
 \le\frac{4C_\Gamma^2}{B}\longrightarrow0.                \tag{12}
\]
Therefore \(B^{-1}\sum_bM_b=o_P(1)\).  Averaging (10), applying (12), and then using \(\texttt{ass:rr-covariance-stabilization}\) proves
\[
 \widehat\Gamma
 =\Omega_{\mathrm{RR}}+B^{-1}\sum_{b=1}^BD_b+o_P(1).       \tag{13}
\]
Again, only \(B\to\infty\) was used.

The deterministic positive-semidefinite averages
\(\bar D_B=B^{-1}\sum_bD_b\) are bounded by (11).  Every subsequence therefore has a further subsequence on which \(\bar D_B\to D_\infty\succeq0\); along that subsequence, (13) yields
\[
 \widehat\Gamma\longrightarrow_P
 \Omega_{\mathrm{RR}}+D_\infty\succeq\Omega_{\mathrm{RR}}. \tag{14}
\]
This proves the asserted Loewner domination of every probability limit point.  More directly, the eigenvalue perturbation inequality, (13), and \(\bar D_B\succeq0\) imply
\[
 \lambda_{\min}(\widehat\Gamma)
 \ge\lambda_{\min}(\Omega_{\mathrm{RR}})+o_P(1).          \tag{15}
\]
Assumption \(\texttt{ass:rr-limit-positive}\) makes the fixed term on the right strictly positive.  Since \(r_B\downarrow0\), (15) shows that clipping is inactive with probability tending to one and
\[
 \|\widehat\Gamma_+^{-1}\|=O_P(1).
\]
This completes both the finite-block identity and the arbitrary-\(G\), many-block concentration claim.

statements.statement:
Along every sequence in \(\mathcal M_{G,B}\) with \(B\to\infty\) and arbitrary admissible even \(G\), including fixed \(G\), the observable ellipse satisfies
\[
\liminf_{B\to\infty}\Pr_{\mathrm{RR}}\{\tau\in\mathcal C_\alpha\}\geq1-\alpha.
\]
statements.justification: The simultaneous region converts the many-block joint law into one operational guarantee for both causal coordinates, with fixed or growing group count.
statements.gap: The prospective Yu--Ma--Liu market design does not supply this history-dependent, positive-semidefinite-completed \(2\)-by-\(2\) joint region under predictable soft rerandomization.
statements.consumer: Market experimenters obtain one simultaneous region for sustained direct and saturation-spillover effects after many randomized blocks.
statements.proof_tex:
Let
\[
 X_B=\sqrt{GB}(\widehat\tau-\tau),
 \qquad
 \bar D_B=B^{-1}\sum_{b=1}^BD_b.
\]
Fix an arbitrary sequence allowed by the proposed statement and then an arbitrary subsequence.  The bound (11) proved in \(\texttt{thm:studentizer}\) makes the deterministic sequence \(\{\bar D_B\}\) bounded in the finite-dimensional space of symmetric \(2\)-by-\(2\) matrices.  It has a further subsequence such that
\[
 \bar D_B\longrightarrow D_\infty
 \quad\text{for some }D_\infty\succeq0.                  \tag{16}
\]
On this further subsequence, \(\texttt{thm:joint-design-clt}\), \(\texttt{thm:studentizer}\), and (16) give
\[
 X_B\Rightarrow X,
 \qquad
 \widehat\Gamma_+\longrightarrow_P\Gamma_\infty,
 \qquad
 X\sim N_2(0,\Omega_{\mathrm{RR}}),
 \quad
 \Gamma_\infty:=\Omega_{\mathrm{RR}}+D_\infty.           \tag{17}
\]
For completeness, the joint convergence implicit in (17) follows without an independence condition: tightness of \(X_B\) permits restriction to a compact set with arbitrarily high probability, and uniform continuity of any bounded continuous test function on that compact set, together with \(\widehat\Gamma_+\to_P\Gamma_\infty\), replaces its second argument by \(\Gamma_\infty\).  The first convergence in (17) then supplies the limit.

Assumption \(\texttt{ass:rr-limit-positive}\) and \(D_\infty\succeq0\) imply that both \(\Omega_{\mathrm{RR}}\) and \(\Gamma_\infty\) are positive definite.  Hence matrix inversion and the quadratic-form map are continuous at every point in the support of the limit in (17), and the same compact-set argument yields
\[
 X_B^\top\widehat\Gamma_+^{-1}X_B
 \Rightarrow X^\top\Gamma_\infty^{-1}X.                  \tag{18}
\]
Write \(X\stackrel d=\Omega_{\mathrm{RR}}^{1/2}Z\), where \(Z\sim N_2(0,I_2)\).  Since \(\Gamma_\infty\succeq\Omega_{\mathrm{RR}}\), inversion reverses Loewner order, and therefore
\[
 0\prec
 H:=\Omega_{\mathrm{RR}}^{1/2}
       \Gamma_\infty^{-1}
       \Omega_{\mathrm{RR}}^{1/2}
 \preceq I_2.                                               \tag{19}
\]
Diagonalize \(H=O\operatorname{diag}(h_1,h_2)O^\top\), where \(0<h_j\le1\).  Rotational invariance of the standard normal and a coupling with the same two normal coordinates give
\[
 X^\top\Gamma_\infty^{-1}X
 \stackrel d=h_1Z_1^2+h_2Z_2^2
 \le Z_1^2+Z_2^2
 \quad\text{almost surely}.                                \tag{20}
\]
The variable on the right has the \(\chi^2_2\) distribution.  The variable on the left of (20) is a sum of two positive multiples of independent squared standard normals and thus has no atom at the positive quantile \(\chi^2_{2,1-\alpha}\).  From (18)--(20),
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \liminf_B\Pr_{\mathrm{RR}}\!\left\{
  X_B^\top\widehat\Gamma_+^{-1}X_B
  \le\chi^2_{2,1-\alpha}\right\}
 &\ge
 \Pr\{Z_1^2+Z_2^2\le\chi^2_{2,1-\alpha}\}\\
 &=1-\alpha.                                                \tag{21}
 \end{aligned}
\]
By \(\texttt{def:simultaneous-wald-region}\), the event in (21) is exactly \(\{\tau\in\mathcal C_\alpha\}\).  If the claimed liminf failed on the original sequence, a violating subsequence would have the further subsequence just analyzed, contradicting (21).  Thus the result holds along every \(B\to\infty\) sequence, without a condition on \(G/B\).

statements.statement: On the boundary extension \(\eta=1\), or equivalently when \(\kappa=0\), \(f_{\eta,\kappa}\equiv1\), \(P_{\mathrm{RR},b}=P_0\), \(v_{\eta,\kappa}=1\), and \(\Omega_{\mathrm{RR}}=\Omega_{\mathrm{CR}}\); the estimator and studentizer reduce to the ordinary balanced two-stage Horvitz--Thompson construction.
statements.justification: The reduction checks that the new design nests its complete-randomization benchmark without altering the causal target.
statements.gap: This is a required sanity reduction rather than a novelty claim.
statements.consumer: Implementers can recover the familiar design by switching off the soft balance penalty.
statements.proof_tex:
Fix a block \(b\) and condition throughout on \(\mathcal F_{b-1}\).  The potential outcomes are fixed, and the only probabilities below are induced by the two stages of the design in \(\mathrm{def:soft\mbox{-}two\mbox{-}stage\mbox{-}design}\).

First consider either of the two boundary cases.  If \(\eta=1\), then for every \(w\in\mathbb R\),
\[
 f_{\eta,\kappa}(w)=1+(1-1)e^{-\kappa w^2}=1.
\]
If \(\kappa=0\), then, using \(0<\eta\leq1\),
\[
 f_{\eta,0}(w)=\eta+(1-\eta)e^0=1.
\]
Thus the two parameter restrictions are equivalent as restrictions on the resulting randomization kernel, although they are not assertions that the parameter values themselves are equal.  In either case, the definition of \(C_b\) gives
\[
 C_b=\mathbb E_0[1\mid\mathcal F_{b-1}]=1,
\]
and consequently, for every \(x\in\mathcal X_G\),
\[
 P_{\mathrm{RR},b}(x\mid\mathcal F_{b-1})
 =P_0(x)\frac{1}{1}=P_0(x).
\]
The division is valid because \(C_b=1>0\).  Since the conditional second-stage law given \(x_b\) in \(\mathrm{def:soft\mbox{-}two\mbox{-}stage\mbox{-}design}\) does not involve \(\eta\) or \(\kappa\), equality of the first-stage laws implies equality of the complete conditional laws of all saturation and treatment indicators under soft rerandomization and balanced complete randomization.

For completeness, this equality also yields the ordinary first-order Horvitz--Thompson weights explicitly.  Because \(G\) is even, the map \(x\mapsto-x\) is a bijection of \(\mathcal X_G\), preserves \(P_0\), and interchanges \(x_g=1\) with \(x_g=-1\).  Hence
\[
 \Pr_0(Q_{gb}=q_H)=\Pr_0(Q_{gb}=q_L)=\frac12.
\]
Conditional on \(Q_{gb}=q\), uniform sampling of exactly \(nq\) units gives
\[
 \Pr(A_{gbi}=d\mid Q_{gb}=q,\mathcal F_{b-1})=p_{dq}.
\]
It follows that
\[
 \pi_{gbi,dq}=\frac12p_{dq}>0,
\]
where positivity follows from \(q_L=1/4\) and \(q_H=3/4\).  Thus the estimator in \(\mathrm{def:joint\mbox{-}ht\mbox{-}estimator}\) is pointwise the balanced two-stage Horvitz--Thompson estimator, with cell weight \(2/p_{dq}\).  Equality of the complete assignment laws also makes every logged pair probability \(\pi_{k\ell,b}\) equal to its complete-randomization value.

We next verify directly that the covariance benchmark also coincides.  Under the just-derived inclusion probabilities, the definitions of \(\widehat\tau_b\) and \(\widehat m_{gbq}\) give
\[
 \widehat\tau_b=\frac2G\sum_{g\in\mathcal G_G}\widehat m_{gb,Q_{gb}}.
\]
The definitions of \(\tau_b\), \(m_{gbq}\), \(e_{gbq}\), and \(a_{gb}\) therefore imply the exact decomposition
\[
 R_b
 =\frac1{\sqrt G}\sum_{g\in\mathcal G_G}x_{gb}a_{gb}
  +\frac2{\sqrt G}\sum_{g\in\mathcal G_G}e_{gb,Q_{gb}}.
\tag{1}
\]
Indeed, the deterministic part of the difference is
\[
 \frac2G\sum_g\left\{\frac{1+x_{gb}}2m_{gbq_H}
 +\frac{1-x_{gb}}2m_{gbq_L}\right\}
 -\frac1G\sum_g(m_{gbq_H}+m_{gbq_L})
 =\frac1G\sum_gx_{gb}a_{gb}.
\]

For each \(q\) and \(d\), the marginal inclusion probability in the uniform fixed-size within-group sample is \(p_{dq}\).  Hence finite-population Horvitz--Thompson algebra gives
\[
 \mathbb E\!\left[
  \frac1n\sum_i\frac{\mathbf1\{A_{gbi}=d\}Y_{gbi}(d,q)}{p_{dq}}
  \mathrel{\Big|}Q_{gb}=q,\mathcal F_{b-1}\right]
 =\frac1n\sum_iY_{gbi}(d,q),
\]
so \(\mathbb E(e_{gbq}\mid Q_{gb}=q,\mathcal F_{b-1})=0\).  The second-stage samples are conditionally independent across groups.  Therefore the two terms in (1) have zero cross-covariance by iterated expectation, and the conditional covariance of the second term, first given \(x_b\) and then averaged over \(P_0\), is
\[
 \mathbb E_0\!\left[
  \frac4G\sum_gT_{gb,Q_{gb}}\mathrel{\Big|}\mathcal F_{b-1}\right]
 =\frac2G\sum_g(T_{gbq_L}+T_{gbq_H})=K_b.
\tag{2}
\]

Complement symmetry gives \(\mathbb E_0x_{gb}=0\).  Exchangeability under the uniform balanced-sign law and the identity \(\sum_gx_{gb}=0\) give, for \(g\neq h\),
\[
 \operatorname{Cov}_0(x_{gb},x_{hb})=-\frac1{G-1},
\]
because
\[
 0=\operatorname{Var}_0\!\left(\sum_gx_{gb}\right)
 =G+G(G-1)\operatorname{Cov}_0(x_{1b},x_{2b}).
\]
Writing \(\bar a_b=G^{-1}\sum_ga_{gb}\), the covariance of the first term in (1) is consequently
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \operatorname{Var}_0\!\left(G^{-1/2}\sum_gx_{gb}a_{gb}
 \mathrel{\Big|}\mathcal F_{b-1}\right)
 &=\frac1G\left\{\sum_ga_{gb}a_{gb}^{\top}
 -\frac1{G-1}\sum_{g\neq h}a_{gb}a_{hb}^{\top}\right\}\\
 &=\frac1{G-1}\sum_g(a_{gb}-\bar a_b)(a_{gb}-\bar a_b)^{\top}.
 \end{aligned}
\tag{3}
\]
Combining (1)--(3) yields
\[
 \operatorname{Var}_0(R_b\mid\mathcal F_{b-1})
 =\frac1{G-1}\sum_g(a_{gb}-\bar a_b)(a_{gb}-\bar a_b)^{\top}+K_b
 =\Sigma_{b,0}.
\]
Since the conditional assignment law under \(P_{\mathrm{RR},b}\) is exactly the same law,
\[
 \Sigma_{b,\mathrm{RR}}
 =\operatorname{Var}_{\mathrm{RR}}(R_b\mid\mathcal F_{b-1})
 =\Sigma_{b,0}
\]
for every block and every finite \(G,B,n\).  Hence the two block-average covariance sequences are termwise identical, and their deterministic limits satisfy
\[
 \Omega_{\mathrm{RR}}=\Omega_{\mathrm{CR}}.
\]

The displayed formula in \(\mathrm{def:projection\mbox{-}gain}\) has a strictly positive denominator in both boundary cases.  Direct substitution gives
\[
 v_{1,\kappa}=\frac{1}{1}=1,
 \qquad
 v_{\eta,0}
 =\frac{\eta+(1-\eta)}{\eta+(1-\eta)}=1,
\]
so the projection gain \((1-v_{\eta,\kappa})P\) is the zero matrix, consistently with the covariance equality.

Finally, \(\widehat\Gamma_b\) in \(\mathrm{def:completed\mbox{-}studentizer}\) is an explicit function only of the realized indicators, observed cell outcomes, and logged first- and second-order inclusion probabilities.  These indicators and inclusion probabilities have exactly their balanced complete-randomization values at either boundary.  Substitution into that displayed formula therefore gives pointwise the ordinary balanced two-stage completed Horvitz--Thompson covariance estimator; averaging over blocks and clipping at the unchanged threshold \(r_B\) preserve this equality.  Thus both \(\widehat\tau\) and \(\widehat\Gamma\) reduce exactly to their ordinary balanced two-stage complete-randomization constructions, which proves the proposition.

statements.statement: The family \(\mathcal W^{AB}\) belongs to \(\mathcal M_{G,B}\), its type A and type B imbalance variances converge to \(53/16\) and \(29/16\), and \[P=\frac12\left\{\frac1{53}\begin{pmatrix}36&6\\6&1\end{pmatrix}+\frac1{29}\begin{pmatrix}4&10\\10&25\end{pmatrix}\right\}\succ0.\] Thus the design is genuinely adaptive through prior observed outcomes and every nonzero joint contrast is strictly improved.
statements.justification: A heterogeneous alternating projection witness establishes that the gain need not be rank one after aggregation and that adaptation is not cosmetic.
statements.gap: Static cluster rerandomization examples use fixed covariates and a fixed projection direction; this family alternates two outcome-adaptive directions while retaining one universal standardized tilt constant.
statements.consumer: It gives simulation designers a falsifiable benchmark whose covariance gain is positive for every direct-spillover contrast.

statements.statement: Let \(\{\xi_{Tt},\mathcal F_{Tt}:1\leq t\leq T\}\) be a square-integrable martingale-difference array, let \(\mathcal V_T=\sum_{t=1}^T\mathbb E(\xi_{Tt}^2\mid\mathcal F_{T,t-1})\), and let \(V_T=\mathbb E(\mathcal V_T)\). If \(\mathcal V_T/V_T=1+o_P(1)\) and, for every \(\epsilon>0\), \(V_T^{-1}\sum_{t=1}^T\mathbb E[\xi_{Tt}^2\mathbf1\{|\xi_{Tt}|\geq\epsilon V_T^{-1/2}\}]=o_P(1)\), then \(V_T^{-1/2}\sum_{t=1}^T\xi_{Tt}\Rightarrow N(0,1)\).

statements.statement:
There exists a deterministic sequence \(\varepsilon_G\downarrow0\) such that, uniformly over blocks, histories, and members of \(\mathcal M_{G,B}\),
\[
\left|\mathbb E_0f_{\eta,\kappa}(W_b)-\mathbb Ef_{\eta,\kappa}(W_b^\star)\right|
+\left\|\mathbb E_0[A_bA_b^\top f_{\eta,\kappa}(W_b)]-\mathbb E[A_b^\star A_b^{\star\top}f_{\eta,\kappa}(W_b^\star)]\right\|
\leq\varepsilon_G,
\]
and
\[
\left\|\mathbb E_0[R_bR_b^\top f_{\eta,\kappa}(W_b)]-\mathbb E[R_b^\star R_b^{\star\top}f_{\eta,\kappa}(W_b^\star)]\right\|
\leq\varepsilon_G.
\]
The comparison is on the exact covariance range and remains valid when the score covariance is singular; no positive lower bound on either score-coordinate variance is required.

For the arrays generated by \(\texttt{def:adaptive-witness}\), using only their displayed bounded construction and the conditional design in \(\texttt{def:soft-two-stage-design}\), uniformly over \(b\in\mathcal B_B\) and every realized history through block \(b-1\),
\[
 \left|\mathbb E_0f_{\eta,\kappa}(W_b)-\mathbb Ef_{\eta,\kappa}(W_b^\star)\right|
 +\left\|\mathbb E_0\{A_bA_b^\top f_{\eta,\kappa}(W_b)\}
 -\mathbb E\{A_b^\star A_b^{\star\top}f_{\eta,\kappa}(W_b^\star)\}\right\|
 \longrightarrow0
\]
as \(G\to\infty\).  The comparison uses the exact covariance range and requires no lower bound on a score-coordinate variance.  Moreover, without using a covariance-stabilization or model-class premise,
\[
 \left\|\Sigma_{b,\mathrm{RR}}-\Sigma_{b,0}
 +(1-v_{\eta,\kappa})\beta_b\beta_b^\top\right\|\longrightarrow0.
\]
statements.justification: This pre-membership comparison breaks the logical cycle between certifying the explicit adaptive witness and invoking the class-level weighted-transport theorem.
statements.gap: The class-level transport theorem applies only after all model-class conditions hold; the witness needs a bounded-array perfect-matching proof before its RR covariance stabilization can be certified.
statements.consumer: The proposition on the alternating adaptive witness uses this lemma to derive RR covariance stabilization and positive definiteness before concluding model-class membership.

sampling_model.design: At each block, condition on \(\mathcal F_{b-1}\), softly tilt the uniform fixed-half saturation assignment by \(f_{\eta,\kappa}(W_b)\), then use independent fixed-count randomization within groups and hold both assignments for two periods.
sampling_model.units: The finite population consists of \(G\) mutually isolated groups of fixed size \(n\), observed at the endpoints of \(B\) two-period blocks; potential outcomes are fixed.
sampling_model.treatment: The first stage assigns exactly \(G/2\) groups to each of \(q_L=1/4\) and \(q_H=3/4\); the second stage treats exactly \(nq\) units within a group assigned saturation \(q\).
sampling_model.overlap: Complement symmetry gives first-stage probability \(1/2\), so every exposure cell has conditional probability \(p_{dq}/2\geq1/8\); feasible pair probabilities are logged and impossible within-group pairs receive PSD completion.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: No superpopulation nuisance is estimated. The randomizer records exact conditional first- and second-order inclusion probabilities, and the analysis uses only observed exposure-cell outcomes.

estimand_functional: \(\widehat\tau=\sum_{d,q}c_{dq}(GBn)^{-1}\sum_{b,g,i}I_{gbi,dq}Y^{\mathrm{obs}}_{g,2b,i}/\pi_{gbi,dq}\), with \(\sqrt{GB}(\widehat\tau-\tau)\Rightarrow N_2(0,\Omega_{\mathrm{RR}})\) along every sequence in \(\mathcal M_{G,B}\) for which \(B\to\infty\), while the admissible even \(G\) may remain fixed or vary arbitrarily with \(B\)

tldr: Predictable soft rerandomization can balance lagged group outcomes without changing the joint sustained direct-and-spillover target. Complement symmetry gives exact first-order propensities, an exact score split isolates the rerandomized balanced-sign component, and a history-uniform singular-support Gaussian transport result would yield both the root-\(GB\) joint limit and the covariance identity \(\Omega_{\mathrm{RR}}=\Omega_{\mathrm{CR}}-(1-v_{\eta,\kappa})P\). Logged pair probabilities and a PSD completion produce an observable conservative \(2\)-by-\(2\) studentizer and simultaneous Wald coverage.

project_justification.gap: Existing papers separately cover static spillover-and-carryover design, sequential balance, general adaptive IPW martingales, and static rerandomization projection geometry. None supplies the history-uniform soft-tilt quadratic-moment transport that joins these layers under fixed-half group saturations and fixed-count within-group assignment.
project_justification.niche: A predictable complement-symmetric kernel preserves exact joint Horvitz--Thompson identification while allowing prior outcomes to improve the precision of sustained direct and spillover effects.
project_justification.fill: The project derives exact unbiasedness, a two-stage martingale/combinatorial central limit theorem, an observable PSD-conservative matrix studentizer, simultaneous coverage, and an explicit projection covariance gain, with the singular weighted Gaussian approximation exposed as the first open theorem step.

related_work: Hudgens--Halloran (2008) and Jiang--Imai--Malani (2023) define and estimate direct and spillover contrasts under static two-stage partial interference. Bojinov--Rambachan--Shephard (2021) supplies the ordinary no-future-assignment nonanticipation convention for dynamic potential outcomes; the stronger lag-one finite-memory equality used here is an imposed restriction tailored to endpoints after two-period held assignments and is not attributed to that paper. Yu--Ma--Liu (2025) adds carryover and a minimax timing design, but its first-stage law is fixed rather than predictably reweighted by prior outcomes. Zhou et al. (2018) optimize sequential covariate balance without spillover or carryover inference. Li--Zhao (2026) provides the adaptive finite-population martingale template, but not dependent two-stage exposure scores. Li--Ding--Rubin (2018) and Lu et al. (2023) give static hard-rerandomization projection geometry. Li--Ding (2017), Shi--Ding (2026), and Tian--Yang--Ding (2025) supply finite-population Gaussian approximation tools, but not radial soft weighting of unbounded score quadratics on singular covariance support. Jizhou Liu (2026) covers static two-stage covariate-adaptive inference, He--Tchetgen Tchetgen (2026) covers broader static two-stage interference, and Liu--Shaikh--Zhong (2026) covers static saturation randomization tests; these current results sharpen the boundary around the proposed outcome-adaptive repeated-block theorem.
technical_internal_limitation: The launch is killed by any bounded legal triangular array for which \(\texttt{oeq:weighted-gaussian-transport}\) fails. Ordinary scalar Berry--Esseen convergence is insufficient because the covariance calculation uses a soft-weighted unbounded quadratic score. Exact enumeration over \(1{,}536\) assignments at \(G=n=4\) checked unbiasedness and the PSD-completion identity only; it is diagnostic evidence, not an asymptotic proof. Pair-probability concentration and the alternating-family uniform history bound remain explicit proof debts.
honest_scope: The estimand is a sustained two-period endpoint contrast under ordinary nonanticipation and an imposed lag-one finite-memory restriction; contemporaneous and carryover components are not separately identified. The population matrix \(P\) depends on unobserved potential-outcome scores through \(\beta_b\), so \(c^\top Pc>0\) is a theoretical characterization and is not claimed to be observable or screenable before deployment without a separate proxy or estimation theorem. The main asymptotics require both \(G\) and \(B\) to grow, predictable covariance stabilization, and \(\lambda_{\min}(\Omega_{\mathrm{RR}})>0\). When the soft tilt is switched off, the construction reduces to ordinary balanced two-stage randomization. The Yu--Ma--Liu market calibration and the Bojinov--Shephard trading experiment are prospective design consumers only; ten historical markets do not validate the growing-\(G\) Gaussian tilt formula.
